result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_edges_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add multiple edges using integer node IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1374-L1498){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_edges_by_id( edges, rel=None, weight=None, **shared_attrs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A strict bulk version of `add_edge_by_id()` that only accepts integer node IDs — no label resolution. All referenced nodes must already exist in the graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Edge definitions to add. Each element can be: - A tuple of `(source_id, target_id)` with shared attributes applied. - A tuple of `(source_id, target_id, attrs_dict)` to override shared attributes. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship type applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional weight applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). [**shared_attrs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attributes applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any source or target is not an integer. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any source or target node ID does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e225d0cc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']) ids = { label: graph.get_id_from_label(label) for label in ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'] } graph.add_edges_by_id( [ (ids['A'], ids['B']), (ids['B'], ids['C']), (ids['C'], ids['D']), ], rel='link' ) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Number of nodes : 4 Number of edges : 3 Directed : True Density : 0.25 Average degree (min, max) : 1.50 (1, 2) Strongly connected : False Weakly connected : True Number of strongly connected components : 4 Number of weakly connected components : 1 ``` ::: ::: Per-edge overrides: ::: {#03135f58 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(['X', 'Y', 'Z']) ids = { label: graph.get_id_from_label(label) for label in ['X', 'Y', 'Z'] } graph.add_edges_by_id( [ (ids['X'], ids['Y']), (ids['Y'], ids['Z'], {'rel': 'strong'}), ], rel='weak' ) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` Number of nodes : 3 Number of edges : 2 Directed : True Density : 0.33 Average degree (min, max) : 1.33 (1, 2) Strongly connected : False Weakly connected : True Number of strongly connected components : 3 Number of weakly connected components : 1 ``` ::: :::
